Blair.note: Three players already voted me out, so I can't tie or get past 3 votes, and my side loses this round regardless. I'll throw nothing so I lose no cards.

Casey.note: I'm Farm, and the hug evidence points at Blair as Meowfia. A Farm throw banks at full value if the target is Meowfia, so I'll stake two high cards on Blair.

Drew.note: I'm dead, but my stake banks at full value if the target is Meowfia. My Kookaburra visit proved Alex is the Mouser, so I'll throw my three highest cards at Alex.

Ellis.note: Voting Blair as the Floofer. I'll throw two 7s and keep my 12s.

Finley.note: Two visitors were hugged after visiting Blair, which only a Floofer does, so Blair is Meowfia. I'll throw my two highest cards at Blair so they bank at full value if I'm right.

Alex.confusing: The Owl and Hawk visit reports were hard to trust because hug and confusion effects made the claims contradict each other, and Blair's Owl claim in round 3 conflicted with the egg rules as I understood them.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: a Tit visit to Finley I reported as Owl started a fight over who was lying, and Casey's Falcon-not-in-play claim gave the table a clear lie to vote on.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports and hug/confusion effects clearer, so players can tell which claims are reliable without guessing.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I pushed hard for Blair while my Meowfia partner Casey was the obvious target, which drew suspicion onto me. I would stay quieter and let the table work through the hug evidence instead.

Blair.confusing: The final score breakdown was hard to follow: "bonus" and "kept" cards weren't explained, so I couldn't tell how the points added up. Confused dawn reports were also hard to trust, since a wrong report can make a true claim look like a lie.
Blair.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: Casey claimed Falcon wasn't in the pool, and Finley's Falcon story kept changing, so the table kept testing each other's claims.
Blair.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about when a report is confused, and show each player's score pile during the game instead of only at the end.
Blair.regret: As the Floofer in Round 3 I visited myself, which hugged the Farm players who visited me and exposed my role. I'd visit a Farm player instead and skip the made-up Owl claim, which the others easily picked apart.

Casey.confusing: The Floofer's hug rule was hard to read: a hugged player only learns their animal did nothing, so two people hugged after visiting Blair pointed at Blair, but the table could not tell whether the hugger was a Floofer or someone else. Pool and role-in-play checks were also easy to get wrong.
Casey.fun: Round 3 was fun: the Hawk and Floofer evidence lined up, and the table converged on Blair as Meowfia, which turned out right.
Casey.change: Make dawn reports say which role visited you when a hug happens, so Floofers and hugged players are easier to pin down.
Casey.regret: In round 2 I openly claimed Sphinx and argued the Falcon point, which exposed my night and drew suspicion. I would have stayed quieter and kept my Sphinx information to myself.

Drew.confusing: The hug mechanic was hard to read: a hugged visitor only learns that their animal did nothing, so several players reasoned from hugs to a Floofer without knowing who the Floofer was. Confused reports also made Blair's claims hard to check.
Drew.fun: Round 1 was fun because Casey's Floofer admission and the two hugs lined up, and the Farm vote on Casey banked my high cards for a 19-point pile.
Drew.change: I would make the dawn reports say whose animal hugged you, or show the Floofer's identity once it is hugged, so players aren't guessing from a single visit.
Drew.regret: In Round 3 I publicly revealed my Kookaburra result on Alex, but that was correct; I would instead have checked Blair's Owl claim against the hugs before piling onto Blair, though it still would have been a Farm win.

Ellis.confusing: The Floofer hug logic was hard to read: a hug only tells you a Floofer visited you, not which visitor was the Floofer, and Blair's Owl claim contradicted the no-visitor egg rule. Several claims also conflicted without a clear way to check them.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: Casey's Floofer hug got exposed, the table converged on a Meowfia, and the banked cards paid off. Watching the Meowfia's false claims unravel was the most satisfying part.
Ellis.change: I'd make the night reports more verifiable, such as showing who visited whom to Farm players, so claims like "I was hugged" can be cross-checked without guessing.
Ellis.regret: None that changes the outcome. In round 2 I could have thrown higher cards at Casey, since the Sphinx claim was clearly false and I was confident in the target.

Finley.confusing: The Floofer's hug mechanic was hard to read: two visitors being hugged points at one player, but a Kookaburra's confusion and the Owl's visit rule made the day's claims hard to check.
Finley.fun: Round 3 was satisfying: the hugs from my Falcon visit and Ellis's Tit visit both pointed at Blair, and the table converged on the right target.
Finley.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about which visitors caused a hug or confusion, so players can check claims without guessing.
Finley.regret: In round 2 I made up a Falcon claim that didn't match my visit, which exposed me as Meowfia. I should have claimed the Mouser role's safe Falcon story from the start, or stayed quiet until the nests were shared.
